comparison.objective: Calibrate a fixed tool tip by touching one reference point from four sufficiently different wrist orientations; candidate instead sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then cycles it to verify retention.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-827 tests precise single-tool pivoting about a stationary contact with stable one-second holds. The candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench seating, bimanual countertorque, setting preservation during jam-nut locking, tool withdrawal, and lever actuation.
comparison.success_condition: PR-827 awards 0.25 per qualified contact pose, requiring four distinct axes for full score. The candidate grades released opening accuracy, installed nut retention, three repeat cycles, limited drift, and one-second tool/gripper clearance, with prerequisite revocation and loss failures.
comparison.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different abilities: multi-orientation TCP contact calibration versus mechanically locking an adjustable stop against tightening reaction and proving hands-off retained motion.
